$comment: Developer-machine settings for working ON this repository.
This is NOT what the server runs. The headless runtime on the server uses
deploy/claude-workspace/settings.json, which is far more restrictive
(read-only, plan mode, no network, no writes). Keeping them separate means
local development is not crippled by production lockdown, and production
lockdown is not loosened by a convenience added during development.
The deny list below is short and deliberate: things that would be a mistake
here regardless of who is asking.
`ssh` was on that list and was removed on 2026-08-08, by the operator, after
it cost a diagnosis. A Telegram bot was crash-looping on the server and the
only way in was through the reviewed scripts, none of which read a journal.
The rule was never a boundary anyway: it matched commands STARTING with ssh,
so every deploy script called ssh internally and passed. What it actually
bought was the habit it named — the server is touched through code that has
been read, tested and versioned, rather than through a command nobody sees
again. That habit is worth keeping without the rule: diagnose freely, but
anything that CHANGES the server still goes through deploy/ or scripts/,
where it can be reviewed and repeated.
`scp` and `git push` stay denied. Neither was asked for, and neither is
needed to diagnose anything.
